idiom_name: Ktor Sessions plugin with server-side storage (SessionStorageMemory, directorySessionStorage, custom SessionStorage)
implementation_notes: Ktor makes both halves of the decision explicit: install(Sessions) { cookie<UserSession>("user_session", SessionStorageMemory()) } stores the payload on the server and passes only the session id to the client, whereas omitting the storage argument would pass the serialized session itself - the choice is per registered cookie or header. Server-side storage options are SessionStorageMemory (in-process, discarded when the server stops), directorySessionStorage for a file under a directory, and the SessionStorage interface (suspend read/write/invalidate) for Redis or a database; handlers use call.sessions.get<UserSession>() / set / clear, and a system property enables deferred retrieval so the store is touched only when a route actually reads the session.
pitfalls: SessionStorageMemory is per process and lost on restart, so a multi-instance deployment silently splits conversations - a custom SessionStorage (Redis, JDBC) is required for a farm.
A custom storage runs on the request coroutine: blocking JDBC or file calls inside read/write block the event loop and must be moved to a dispatcher.
Forgetting clear() on logout leaves the record in the storage until its timeout; the session id is re-issued but the old payload stays readable if it leaks.
